solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fool sailors, when aboard

indicators.note: being aboard means being carried inside a vessel, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: jacks (jack tars) are sailors
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at clumsy sailors once they have come on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's name used as an insult for a stupid person, so it is a synonym of fool.

clue.text: Carol, beautiful girl heard cutting catchy tunes

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the tunes word, so the girl sits inside it

parts.note: jingles are short catchy tunes, as in advertising

indicators.note: heard means the word for a beautiful girl is used for its sound

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl

explanation.surface: A girl named Carol, a beauty, is heard interrupting some catchy songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a girl's name; it means a Christmas song.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous Christmas song, so an example of a carol.

clue.text: Artist received by court upset museum administrator?

indicators.note: received by means the artist is taken inside the other letters
upset signals the letters of court are knocked into a new order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter turns up at a court that is distressed, much to the museum boss's concern.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator looks after a collection of exhibits; the question mark admits not all are administrators.

clue.text: Result of bumpkin being caught by a belt?

definitions.text: Result of bumpkin being caught by a belt?

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the bumpkin goes within the word for belt

parts.note: to belt or tear is to rush along at speed
a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A yokel hit with a punch ends up with a swollen ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' reads as a punch for the whole clue but in the wordplay means to tear along fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen ear from a blow is the idiomatic result of a cuff round the head.

clue.text: Beginning to scare me about revolutionary's plot

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first two pieces wrap around the revolutionary
beginning to means only the first letter of scare is used

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's plot starts to frighten the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan, and a scheme is the same sort of scheming design.

clue.text: Good to have evening dress

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Advice that it is good to own something smart to wear in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A long formal dress worn to evening events is a gown, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Stone in part of Stonehenge, massive

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters within these words

explanation.surface: A stone sits in part of the huge prehistoric monument.
explanation.walkthrough: Stonehenge is a prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone, cut and polished as jewellery, is a gem.

clue.text: Has a job in factory

definitions.meaning: to be employed is to be labouring at a job
a factory is an industrial plant, as in gasworks

explanation.surface: Someone is employed at a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is employed labours for pay, and an industrial plant is also called this.

clue.text: Somewhat unorthodox former prime minister

indicators.note: somewhat suggests only some of the word unorthodox is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Describing a past British premier as a bit of a maverick.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was British prime minister from 1770 to 1782, during the loss of the American colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick, Lord North, led the British government as prime minister in the 18th century.

clue.text: Bone china defaced? Certain to be returned

indicators.note: defaced here means losing its face, the front letter

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a chum

indicators.note: returned means the word for certain is read backwards

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone damaged their bone china and insists it must go back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone china' looks like one phrase; 'Bone' is the definition and 'china' means a friend in rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: This is the long bone of the upper arm, running from shoulder to elbow.

clue.text: Develop film, producing computer program

parts.note: to spread is to develop or extend
a sheet is a thin film or layer

explanation.surface: Processing a photographic film turns out a piece of software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Develop film' suggests photography; both words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Excel and its rivals are grid-based applications for calculation, a kind of computer software.

clue.text: Allow the Parisian time

parts.note: le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A request to give a Parisian some time.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to let it happen, so these are synonyms.

clue.text: Former Soviet official given order by young woman in automobile

indicators.note: in places the order and the young woman within the vehicle word

parts.note: car is a synonym of automobile
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A Soviet functionary receives a decoration from a girl sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: In the USSR a commissar was a Communist Party official, so a former Soviet functionary.

clue.text: Crime committed with collusion — behind bars affair

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
a job is an affair or matter

explanation.surface: A crime done with help from within lands the culprits in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A theft carried out with help from someone on the staff is the classic term.

clue.text: Fast food item, food rejected by her, heading off

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for food is read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter, the head, is removed from the word her

explanation.surface: A takeaway snack is passed over by a woman who then leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamburger in a bun is the classic fast-food item sold by chains.

clue.text: Bad hats confronting the old lady making a complaint

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of hats are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: old lady is slang for one's mother, so MA

explanation.surface: Mum confronted by hideous headgear, which she grumbles about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grumble, but here it means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean a medical condition, and this respiratory illness is one example.

clue.text: Wary, he worried about one getting completely out of control

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go round the one
worried signals the letters of wary he are shaken into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cautious man frets that someone is spiralling out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, things that go this way become chaotic and erratic, entirely out of hand.

clue.text: Importance of data around university

indicators.note: around means the data word goes round the university letter

parts.note: stats, statistics, are data

explanation.surface: How much a university's data matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or prestige, so the importance someone carries.

clue.text: Rebuked on island after fifty set free

indicators.note: after sends the island letter second, behind the fifty numeral
on means the rebuke word is attached next, following the island

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
berated means rebuked, told off

explanation.surface: Someone scolded on an island, after turning fifty, is finally released.
explanation.definitionFit: To be freed from captivity or control is to be liberated, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rubbish left in large one, ultimately

indicators.note: in means the left letter goes inside the word for large

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Junk left behind inside a large container, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is nonsense, worthless talk, an informal synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Whiskeys, right away? Certainly

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of the drinks

parts.note: ryes are rye whiskeys

explanation.surface: Asking for whiskies straight away and getting an emphatic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whiskeys' suggests the NATO alphabet's W, but it is RYES, rye whiskeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying certainly is an emphatic affirmative, the same as a plain word of agreement.

clue.text: Conspicuous foreigner in street

indicators.note: in places the foreigner word inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: An outsider stands out noticeably on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Something salient stands out and is the most noticeable, hence conspicuous.

clue.text: The Spanish king will get large deer

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: The king of Spain is to receive a big stag.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk is the largest member of the deer family.

clue.text: Petrol, or electricity, in essence

definitions.meaning: informal for fuel or electric power
the ... of something is its extracted essence

explanation.surface: Fuel and power are basically the same thing at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for power or fuel, and also the extract or essential liquid of something.

clue.text: Lacking strength, reportedly, for seven days

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: weak means lacking strength

explanation.surface: Feeling feeble, as it is said, for a whole week.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven days make up one calendar unit, the period from one Monday to the next.

clue.text: National topic

definitions.meaning: a national of a country is a citizen of that state
a topic is the matter under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: A citizen is a subject of a state, and a theme of discussion is its subject matter.
